title: A failed build_strategy_evidence.py run OVERWRITES a committed MEASURED record with a harness_failed stub — two real measurements were nearly lost
note: OBSERVED by the E41 lane 2026-09-22, not inferred: its first run of scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py DESTROYED the committed `measured` records for gld_pullback_1d and qqq_trend_long_1d, nulling net_r_oos, n_trades_oos and fold_detail and replacing them with a harness_failed stub. The cause was mundane — yfinance was absent from the sandbox — and that is the point: an ordinary environment gap silently converts evidence into a stub. THEY SURVIVED ONLY BECAUSE THE LANE READ `git diff` BEFORE COMMITTING. On a different day that is two measurements gone, with the commit looking like a routine regeneration. [!] WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A SCRIPT BUG: comms/strategy_evidence/ IS the corpus B1's four-clause bar reads to decide whether a leg may reach a real-money roster, and a harness_failed stub does not read as a loss — it reads as a leg that was never measured. That is the collapsed state this repo files bugs about (`we could not look` rendered identically to `we looked and found nothing`), sitting on the promotion path. [!] THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SHAPE IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: a failed run must never overwrite a record that currently reads `measured`. Write the failure somewhere it is visible (a separate field, a refusal, a non-zero exit) but leave the measurement intact, and make the refusal LOUD rather than a silent skip. Whether a re-measure may overwrite a measured record when it SUCCEEDS is a different question and stays as it is. [!] AND TWO SIBLINGS FILED BY THE SAME LANE BELONG WITH IT, because they are the same artifact lying about itself: PI-20260922-E41-0005 — qqq's record claims `fidelity: faithful` with `omitted_levers: []` while its harness run omits tp_r entirely, and the README defines faithful as 'modelled EVERY lever the leg's config declares'. Not cosmetic: the omitted lever is the one that moved that leg's number 3.4x (net_r_oos 1.9389 -> 6.6307 on an identical data span, the ONLY difference being arm 3.56 -> 0.0). PI-20260922-E41-0006 carries a prediction registered IN ADVANCE — re-run with tp_r modelled and the two should agree; if they do not, the inert-by-construction reasoning behind the qqq arm strip is wrong and #12737 needs re-opening. resolution_criteria: a planted harness failure against a committed measured record leaves the record BYTE-IDENTICAL and exits non-zero; the fidelity claim is computed from what the run actually modelled rather than asserted; and 0006's prediction is either confirmed or recorded as refuted. [!] MERGE REPAIR 2026-09-22T17:4xZ (manager, session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH). Three scalars restored by hand after the register merge driver took them from the wrong side on this branch's merge of origin/main -- the defect filed as PI-20260922-JN54P2HH-0002, which merges NOTES correctly and then takes `state`/`prs`/`blocked_on` from whichever side had the longer note. E28 read `landed_unproven` on the merged tree against `done` on main. E5 read `queued` with `prs: []` on MAIN ITSELF -- that one is not this branch's regression, it is the same defect landing earlier and going unrepaired, so the operator's live Workflow page has been showing a finished lane as unstarted. E46 was carrying no PR link for #12754. VERIFIED by diffing every row of the merged tree against origin/main on state/status/prs/blocked_on/owner/next_action and on note LENGTH, not by eye. [!] CLOSE-OUT TRUE-STATE PASS, 2026-09-22T18:4xZ, manager session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH. Was `in_flight` with no PR link; the lane (session_01AtmcbUvFuN6GThPjvBLxLA) is archived and #12754 MERGED. Set to landed_unproven, not done, because the row's own resolution_criteria names an observation nobody has made: a planted harness failure against a committed MEASURED record must leave that record BYTE-IDENTICAL and exit non-zero, the fidelity claim must be computed from what the run actually modelled rather than asserted, and 0006's prediction must be confirmed or recorded as refuted.
